Welcome back! Anthropic published the requests it had to block, OpenAI asked Congress to regulate it on a bad day for the timing, and NASA now has a model that hunts for ice on the Moon.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Claude was asked to help build bioweapons: Which pathogens came up, and who was doing the asking? OpenAI shipped two products for people who don't use ChatGPT: What finally kills the phone menu that outlived four decades of technology? NASA and IBM built an AI foundation model for the Moon: What is it looking for in the craters that never see sunlight? OpenAI is asking Congress to regulate it: What did Reuters publish the same day? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Claude was asked to help build bioweapons Anthropic released a new threat intelligence report describing attempts to use its models for biological and conventional weapons research. The cases are specific.  Researchers asked Claude for help with gain-of-function work involving chikungunya and with assessing the pandemic potential of avian influenza.  In one instance the researchers were working at a military research institute outside the United States.  Anthropic says its safeguards blocked some of the requests and triggered internal investigations. The report also covers six cases tied to conventional weapons development, with activity linked to China, Russia and Yemen. Anthropic banned the accounts involved, disrupted the networks being used to get around regional restrictions and shared what it found with governments and other AI companies. The pattern underneath is the one the whole industry has to deal with.  A model that speeds up legitimate biology speeds up the other kind too, and the difference between the two is often the intent of whoever is typing. 78952.subject: Robinhood Chain Cashes In
78952.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Happy Friday. Markets head into today’s CPI print on shaky footing as higher oil prices and rising odds of a rate hike dragged BTC, gold and equities lower. ETHFI was the exception, gaining 14.8% as EtherFi Cash continued to post record volumes and grow its share of protocol revenue.

Meanwhile, Robinhood Chain has already blown past our expectations. It generated $38.8M in REV over just 15 days, briefly reaching a $944M annualized run rate. We revisit whether that surge can last and what it could mean for Robinhood’s broader crypto business.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

All four major benchmarks finished the day in the red. The S&P 500 fell 0.73% and the Nasdaq declined 1.34%, while gold and BTC both lost 1.87%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6c74bd3d-a837-4219-b68f-b1dc6113c213/image.png?t=1789129663)
Caption: 

The weakness largely came down to changing interest rate expectations. The odds of a hike next week have risen to [66.7%](https://www.investing.com/central-banks/fed-rate-monitor), up from 52.4% a week ago. Renewed hostilities between the US and Iran have pushed oil above $100, adding to inflationary pressure and strengthening the case for the Fed to keep policy tight.

The US bond market also [sold off](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-corrected-2026-09-11/) after the Treasury’s buyback fell short of the expected $6B. Together, higher oil prices, rising yields and a more hawkish rate outlook created a difficult backdrop for risk assets. Some of yesterday’s selling may also reflect investors reducing exposure ahead of today’s CPI release, which could materially shift expectations for next week’s Fed decision.

The weakness extended across crypto, with Crypto Equities the only sector to finish modestly higher.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d1478182-c5b1-49cf-8bdc-2fed658979a7/image.png?t=1789129663)
Caption: 

However, one token stood out in the sea of red. ETHFI gained 14.8% as EtherFi Cash continued to post record weekly volumes and revenue extended its recovery from the June lows. Cash now generates around 60% of EtherFi’s revenue, yet the market continues to value ETHFI primarily as a liquid restaking token. 🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-off grips crypto: a hot PPI print and surging bond yields knocked Bitcoin below $77K as traders brace for CPI and next week's Fed decision. Yet the institutional plumbing keeps expanding — from SGX and Kalshi perps to MoneyGram's stablecoin card. 📉 Bitcoin Sinks Below $77K as Hot PPI Revives Fed Rate-Hike Fears A hotter-than-expected 5.4% August PPI reading and Brent crude above $107 drove US bond yields to fresh multi-decade highs, dragging Bitcoin under $77,000 and triggering roughly $456M in mostly-long liquidations. Crypto equities fared worse, with Coinbase off about 5% and Strategy down around 7%, as attention turned to Friday's CPI and the September 15–16 Fed meeting. Read full story → ⚖️ Kalshi Plans 24/7 Tesla, Apple and Nvidia Perpetual Futures Prediction-market operator Kalshi intends to seek approval for about 60 perpetual futures tied to major stocks and ETFs — which would be the first regulated single-stock perps in the US. The plan set off a jurisdictional fight after Citadel Securities told the SEC and CFTC that moving equity-linked perps outside SEC oversight could create a parallel shadow market with weaker safeguards against insider trading. More details → 🏛️ SGX Opens Bitcoin and Ether Perps to US Institutions Singapore Exchange secured CFTC authorization under Regulation 48.10 to let US institutional investors trade its Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures directly, bridging American trading desks with Asian liquidity pools. The contracts have logged about $5.8 billion in cumulative volume since launching in late November 2025, with dated futures and options next in the pipeline. Read more → 🐶 Bitwise to Liquidate Its Dogecoin ETF After Less Than a Year Bitwise is winding down its spot Dogecoin ETF (BWOW), with a final NYSE trading day expected October 14 and cash distributions to remaining holders on October 22 — roughly 10 months after launch. The fund held only around $722,000 in assets and fell about 45% since inception, a blunt reminder that ETF access does not guarantee investor demand.
